lenses.verification_red_team: C1: release date 25 Nov per Hershey Co. blog, Marketing Dive and Rotten Tomatoes (Wikipedia says 26 Nov — minority, use 25). Scores 17%/90% are early and small (18 reviews, 100+ ratings) and will move: label 'early scores, 27 Nov'. No source gives budget, funder or box office: never say 'Hershey paid for' or 'hit'. 'Refusal to advertise' is Britannica; Wikipedia notes he still used unconventional promotion (painted delivery car, 1927 film placement in Wings) — so say 'refused to advertise' as his stance, and avoid 'never promoted anything'. Quote 'Give them quality...' via Biography.com. Failures: Philadelphia shop failed/bankruptcy (Britannica, Hershey Co.), NY failed (Britannica). $1,000,000 sale in 1900 (Britannica, Wikipedia). Caramel founding year conflicts — omit. 5-cent tie-in: 'at their original 5-cent price' (Marketing Dive); duration of the 5-cent price not sourced — omit. 1970 national advertising date not confirmed — omit.
lenses.audience_psychology: Irony is the hook: the anti-ad founder becomes a 90-minute ad and people choose to watch. Everyone knows the chocolate; few know he went broke first. The critic/audience split gives a clean conflict and lets the viewer pick a side. Share test: 'Hershey made a movie about itself and critics hate it but audiences love it' — yes. Persian audience: Hershey's is a recognised imported chocolate; the founder-fails-then-wins arc travels across cultures.
lenses.brand_fit: Pure brand strategy: storytelling vs advertising, founder story as brand asset, content marketing. Owner lesson: the story customers pay attention to is the struggle, not the boast; show the failure you hide. Fits Behnood's strategist voice; avoids repeating AI-ad, borrowed-fame and naming topics.
